svg.text: Draining executor A (group G restarts in place)
Executors hold no streams, so draining one only moves leases. Streams stay open on gateways and pause for milliseconds.
1 · Stop signal
roster state = draining (gateways and peers stop placing on A) · stop claiming · keep serving every session A still owns
2 · Sessions, cheapest first (a session that just received a round jumps the queue)
Cold
nothing in memory
→ RELEASE
node_id = '', 1 statement; the next
round's preferred executor claims it
Everything else — including steps that are still streaming
→ HANDOFF: PREPARE (+ step buffers) · pause · TRANSFER · COMMIT to B
a streaming step keeps running on its dispatch gateway; its next deltas, events and result go to B
PA streams stay subscribed to S's channel; B publishes there now, so they pause for milliseconds
only wait: a durable write or a dispatch start in progress (milliseconds)
successor ∉ G: a draining executor refuses PREPARE
3 · Deadline (25 s, inside the platform stop timeout)
TRANSFER whatever is left to its HRW successors (pending work is never released) · later arrivals get NOT_OWNER(B)
4 · Delete roster row, exit
the control channel stays open until the last handoff
5 · Restart: same address, new node_id
leftovers claimable at once · same member_name →
same placement
